abstract: Splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTL) remain less explored than expression QTL (eQTL) in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We mapped cis-eQTL and cis-sQTL in 1,149 colon samples from SPARC IBD participants in IBD Plexus, identifying 20,566 genes with eQTL (eGenes) and 9,906 with sQTL (sGenes). Colocalization prioritized 239 eGenes and 164 sGenes across 147 of 320 IBD risk loci, including 58 genes supported by both traits. We assessed candidate splicing consequences involving nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), 5' untranslated region remodeling, and protein domain alteration. In five genes with GWAS-colocalized eQTL and sQTL, risk alleles were associated with reciprocal changes in total gene expression and usage of junctions linked to predicted NMD-sensitive transcripts, consistent with NMD. IBD-associated sGenes were enriched in immune and inflammatory pathways and included drug targets. These findings motivate investigation of whether genotype-associated splicing differences, particularly those predicted to alter protein domains, contribute to variation in responses to IBD therapies.
